Appendix.title: Phase 28 - Systems From Emulator to Trust - Visual Recall
Appendix.source: Visual Recall/Phase 28 - Systems From Emulator to Trust - Visual Recall.md
Appendix.Content: Systems recall — one snapshot from executed byte to trusted replay

This is a reconstruction companion, not a replacement for the continuous systems teaching. Start with the user loading a cartridge, making a snapshot and attempting a remote restore. Follow causal operations in order and reconstruct the reason for every byte and lifetime boundary.
Rebuild the emulated CPU

Given an NROM image containing one 16-KiB PRG bank and a reset vector pointing to $8000, trace the file/header offsets, PRG bank mapping to CPU <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>8000</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> </math>C000, the bytes read at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>F</mi> <mi>F</mi> <mi>F</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> </math>FFFD, the PC after reset, and the first opcode fetch. Explain why a raw 65536-byte array cannot replicate PPU/controller/mapper I/O side effects. Define the minimal state machine S(t+1)=T(S(t),input(t)) and identify the missing state if only A/X/Y/PC are saved.

Trace ADC $7F+$01 with C=0. The 8-bit result is $80, carry is clear, signed overflow and negative are set. Trace $FF+$01: $00 with carry and zero set but signed overflow clear. Derive the overflow formula from operand/result sign bits rather than memorizing it. Then decode BNE relative: the signed 8-bit displacement is added to PC after the operand is fetched; a taken branch incurs a cycle and a page crossing may incur another.

Explain why a controller shift register is stateful I/O, why a simplified OAM page copy does not prove 513/514-cycle DMA timing, and why accumulating 3 PPU dots per CPU tick cannot implement VBlank, odd-frame skip or sprite evaluation.
Reproduce the C++20 CPU oracle and identify its explicitly unsupported behavior before claiming any emulator accuracy beyond the tested subset.
Rebuild a safe state transfer

Design a versioned save-state record without writing native struct bytes. Describe each field’s representation and endian convention, reject malformed version/length before mutation, and name all missing device states needed for complete replay. Show how an atomic temporary-file publication differs from a stream flush and from crash durability. Include the file/directory sync policy for the chosen platform and a plan for interrupted/short writes.

Define a length-prefixed TCP frame parser whose length bytes arrive separately. Prove it does not read uninitialized data or allocate more than the maximum permitted message size. Explain why UDP can drop, reorder or duplicate datagrams while TCP has no application message boundaries. Draw the timeline of a predicted input tick, a delayed authoritative acknowledgment and deterministic replay of unacknowledged commands. State the exact source of divergence if the client and server physics use inconsistent iteration order.
Rebuild the trust boundary

Distinguish SHA-256, HMAC and authenticated encryption in terms of the problem each solves. Write the symbolic HKDF extract/expand recurrence and name the context separation role of info. Explain why a digest displayed alongside a file cannot prove its origin when an attacker can replace both.

Derive why an AES-GCM nonce must remain unique for a key even across process restarts. Give a failure-injection plan for corrupt ciphertext, wrong AAD, truncated tags, replay and crash during nonce-counter persistence. Do not invent a homebrew encryption implementation; identify the cryptographic library and API contracts that would be verified first.

For a Shamir threshold (t,n) scheme, express the random polynomial over a finite field and derive reconstruction of the constant coefficient at x=0. Explain why fewer than t shares are information-theoretically insufficient only under the stated randomness assumptions. For a Merkle inclusion proof, list the sibling hashes/positions required to reconstruct a trusted root and explain why a valid proof says nothing about whether the root itself is authentic.

Cross Rust/Python/native boundaries with a pointer: name its owner, lifetime, allocation/deallocation domain, thread restrictions and error/panic conversion. Then create an allow/redact/deny policy for a remote snapshot and specify what information is preserved in an audit log without leaking secrets.
Evidence and mastery gate

Do not mark all 100 parts as executed just because the CPU lab compiles. M163–M164 have a constrained executable CPU/bus/NROM witness. M165–M168 have connected explanation and primary-source references, but still require filesystem, network, established-cryptography and FFI integration tests. A complete mastery demonstration reconstructs and falsifies the entire byte-to-trusted-replay pipeline under partial failures, not merely a successful load of one synthetic ROM.

Appendix.title: Phase 4 - CPU, Memory and Job Systems - Visual Recall
Appendix.source: Visual Recall/Phase 4 - CPU, Memory and Job Systems - Visual Recall.md
Appendix.Content: One scene update across the machine — Phase 4 retrieval

This is a reconstruction companion, not a replacement for the first and second continuous chapters. All 100 canonical titles and their actual proof limits appear in the source contract. Each task below asks for a causal proof or independent implementation; reading the attached answer is not an assessment.
Reconstruction A — from source to instruction schedule

A particle loop loads x and mass, multiplies them and accumulates into one scalar. Construct a dependency graph showing which loads can overlap and why the accumulator creates a true dependency. Explain why superscalar width is not achieved throughput. Consider what happens if the loop is unrolled into four independent partial accumulators: register pressure rises; dependence depth may shrink; floating-point sum order changes. Distinguish a branch predictor’s speculation from the C++ semantics that decide which results are architecturally visible. Sketch a hypothetical five-stage pipeline, then identify what the model omits about modern out-of-order execution.
Required evidence: an optimized assembly excerpt, compiler version/flags and a separate handwritten baseline. If you cannot show them, do not claim a measured instruction cost.
Reconstruction B — where the 64-byte record goes

A large AoS record has sixteen float components, but the hot loop reads only two of them. Derive the useful-byte fraction under a 64-byte-line illustrative cache. Compare the address sequence with separate x/mass arrays. Compute the 64 sets of a hypothetical 32-KiB, 8-way, 64-byte-line cache, and design a repeating stride that can produce conflicts under its simple index mapping. Explain why L1/L2/L3 latency, DRAM bandwidth, TLB misses and NUMA placement are different possible bottlenecks. Give a test that could disprove the hypothesis SoA is always faster.
Required evidence: identical numerical results plus repeated timing and counters on a specified CPU. The current lab proves only selected equality and an optional timing experiment.
Reconstruction C — why false sharing is not a data race

Two workers update two distinct atomic counters. Explain how a coherence unit covering both counters may migrate, even if both threads use race-free atomic increments. Compare this with two workers writing the same ordinary integer without synchronization (undefined behavior). Derive why alignas(64) can help on a machine with appropriate interference granularity but does not guarantee an arbitrary platform’s cache-line size. Explain how a store-release plus observing load-acquire publishes a non-atomic payload, and give a counterexample where the acquire load does not observe the publishing value.
Required evidence: coherent happens-before argument, with actual source atomic orders and object lifetime. A passing run alone cannot establish the absence of all possible data races.
Reconstruction D — storage acquisition is not object construction

Design a 4-KiB bounded arena for 64-byte aligned scratch records. Compute padding, capacity and overflow checks before producing a pointer. Explain when placement construction starts object lifetime, which destructors must run, and why monotonic allocation cannot be treated as a per-object free list. Compare slab, buddy, size-class, LIFO stack, free-list and frame arenas for a mixed workload of transient commands and persistent mesh records. Distinguish internal and external fragmentation.

Then trace a mesh whose CPU handle is erased while a GPU draw might still use its underlying buffer. Explain how a monotonic completion timeline permits physical destruction only after the actual submitted use finishes. Analyze what must change for multiple GPU queues or device loss. The CPU ticket model is not a Vulkan or Metal implementation.
Reconstruction E — make three threads progress without a lost wake-up

Implement one task queue with mutex and condition variable. Write the exact shared predicate checked in a loop; explain why checking a condition once or relying solely on notify_one is insufficient under spurious wakes or races. Prove that workers release the lock before executing user tasks. Consider a dependency chain A→B→C and show how workers waiting synchronously for tasks from the same saturated pool may deadlock. Distinguish deadlock, livelock and starvation; construct an explicit circular lock-order counterexample.

Implement one producer publishing a payload through store-release and one consumer reading it after observing load-acquire. Distinguish relaxed counter increments from this publication protocol. Explain how compare-and-exchange can encounter ABA and why generation tags are not a general memory reclamation scheme.
Reconstruction F — work/span, deterministic sums and profiler evidence

Given W units of work and S on the critical path, derive the ideal bounds T_P ≥ max(W/P,S). For a task cost c and scheduling overhead h, explain why increasing the number of tasks improves balancing until overhead and contention dominate. Compare a shared queue with a per-worker work-stealing deque, including the single-item steal race that needs a real algorithmic protocol. With ten thousand exact integer-valued doubles, demonstrate fixed partitioning and ordered reduction; then exhibit three floating-point numbers whose reassociation changes the result.

Starting from a hypothetical 16-ms frame breakdown, form one falsifiable hypothesis. Choose a sampling profiler, instrumentation trace or hardware counters appropriate to the hypothesis. State warm-up, sample count, cache conditions, confidence/variance, end-to-end measurement and rollback condition. Derive Amdahl speedup for serial fraction 0.2 and four ideal workers: 2.5, not 4. Then explain which model assumptions would fail for real heterogeneous CPU/GPU execution.
End-to-end mastery gate

Reconstruct the entire asset-to-frame chain without looking at the book: a typed catalog retains an owned resource; a hot loop chooses AoS or SoA from actual accesses; the compiler emits an instruction schedule; threads share memory only through defined synchronization; a persistent pool executes independent jobs while dependencies constrain progress; scratch memory remains alive through its users; GPU resources cannot retire before completion; a profiler establishes whether the optimization truly improves the frame. Name every assumption, uncertainty and failure path. If the real Kairo/Maveb code is uninspected, say so rather than claiming correspondence.

Research and source bridge: MIT 6.172, Agner Fog’s manuals, cppreference atomics, and Amdahl’s 1967 paper. These references establish concepts and comparison methods; they do not establish the current engine’s measured results.
One lane, three arithmetic contracts

For unsigned eight-bit lanes, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>250</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>260</mn> </math>: wrap → 4; saturate → 255; widen → 260. A lane’s discarded carry never increments the next lane. A portable scalar loop can verify these values without proving SIMD instruction selection or speed.

Recall: why can ordinary signed C++ overflow not be justified by a hardware wrapping instruction? The language expression’s promoted type and range still govern it. Work the second four-lane exercise, then check the complete trace, solution and commented scalar oracle.

Appendix.title: Phase 5 - Algorithms by Workload - Visual Recall
Appendix.source: Visual Recall/Phase 5 - Algorithms by Workload - Visual Recall.md
Appendix.Content: An asset request becomes a data structure, graph and scheduling decision

This companion tests independent reconstruction, not recognition of terminology. The full, concept-led teaching runs from the asset data model to navigation, sorting, scans and caches. All exact original parts and which of them have executable evidence are in the contract ledger. The test reference is the standalone C++20 lab.
The first decision: what is the abstract promise?

The editor must look up a mesh name, enumerate assets in sorted order, update component storage, process streaming requests and repeatedly find the next shortest tentative route. Describe the operations and required ordering separately, then choose a concrete representation. Explain why a map, ordered map, vector, ring, priority queue and sparse set are different answers even when they all store references to the same assets. Derive a Big-O bound using an explicit input size and constants, then explain why this bound does not predict cache-miss or allocator cost.

Answer to verify against: A workload chooses an ADT first, and that ADT defines operations. Different representations implement the ADT with different time, space, invalidation and ordering properties. Expected hashing cost requires a distribution/quality assumption; tree worst-case cost requires a balancing invariant. The Phase 4 hardware model supplies the missing locality and bandwidth dimensions.
Dynamic storage and wraparound

Derive the geometric series showing that vector’s O(n) occasional relocation leads to O(1) amortized append across n appends under geometric capacity growth. Explain why the worst-case one append remains O(n), and which iterators or pointers reallocation invalidates. Then implement a fixed-capacity ring that distinguishes full from empty without one permanently unused slot. Trace: push 10,20,30; reject 40; pop 10,20; push 40,50; pop 30,40,50. State where object lifetimes begin and end when ring slots contain nontrivial types.

Answer to verify against: Store head and count, with tail=(head+count) mod C and 0≤count≤C. The lab uses optional slot values; this is a single-thread FIFO, not a correct multi-producer lock-free ring. A deque or linked list offers different mutation/iterator contracts.
A hash collision is an algorithm, not a rare exception

Draw a table where keys 1,9,17 collide under modulo-eight indexing. Place entries using linear probing, delete one in the middle, then show why an unoccupied tombstone cannot terminate a later lookup. Design insertion that remembers a tombstone but still searches for a duplicate key farther along the chain. Distinguish linear probing, quadratic probing, Robin Hood displacement, separate chaining and immutable perfect hashing; explain when each requires rehashing or special deletion rules.

Answer to verify against: A never-used slot terminates a probe chain; a tombstone does not. The lab includes growth and 1,200 reproducible mutations compared to std::unordered_map. It does not claim Robin Hood or perfect hashing is implemented. Expected constant-time performance is conditional.
A probabilistic structure makes a one-sided claim

Derive the Bloom filter approximate false-positive probability (1−e(−kn/m))k and state the independence/uniformity assumption. A query whose kth bit is zero proves absence under a no-deletion contract; all-one bits permit a false positive. Explain why clearing a shared bit on deletion can create a false negative for another inserted key. Compare Bloom membership with exact bitsets and exact hashed sets.
Answer to verify against: Never assert that Bloom query positives prove membership. The lab only asserts no false negatives for known inserted keys.
Tree invariants and heaps

Explain why an unbalanced BST can degenerate from O(log n) to O(n), and reconstruct one AVL rotation preserving in-order traversal. State the red-black invariants that bound tree height. Compare a B-tree and B+ tree in terms of block/page accesses and range scans. Now trace binary-heap insertion into an array, list its parent and child indices and show why the heap property is weaker than global sorted order. Explain why a priority queue supports Dijkstra even if it allows stale entries.

Answer to verify against: AVL/red-black/B+/radix implementations are not in the current lab; independent adversarial insertion/deletion oracles are still required. The lab uses a standard-library heap to test actual graph distances.
From graph meaning to valid paths

Construct one directed four-vertex graph with weights 0→1=2, 0→2=5, 1→2=1, 1→3=10 and 2→3=1. Trace BFS hops, Dijkstra distances, Bellman–Ford relaxations, A* g/h/f values and Floyd–Warshall D_k updates. Explain why BFS returns hop counts [0,1,1,2] while Dijkstra returns [0,2,3,4]. Add a negative edge and show why Dijkstra’s greedy proof fails. Then create a reachable negative cycle and show how one extra Bellman–Ford relaxation detects it.

Answer to verify against: Nonnegative weights are essential for Dijkstra’s usual correctness argument; A* requires an admissible heuristic for optimality under the stated algorithm/termination rules, and consistency provides an additional edgewise inequality. The lab’s A* does not certify a caller-supplied heuristic. Floyd–Warshall is an independent O(V³) oracle on bounded small graphs, not necessarily the best production navigator.
Directed dependencies and undirected connectivity

Draw a pass DAG. Compute indegrees and perform Kahn’s topological sort. Add an edge from the final node to the first and explain why no topological order can exist. Then describe SCC condensation and why cycles require an explicit feedback/error policy rather than a lucky traversal order. For an undirected weighted graph, trace Kruskal’s sorted edges and DSU unions and justify the selected edge using the cut property. Compare to Prim without mistaking an MST for shortest paths.

Answer to verify against: The graph lab detects cycles, computes an MST of cost six and tests DSU unions. It does not implement all SCC and Prim variants; those require additional implementation witnesses.
When integer order becomes a buffer-offset proof

From counts [3,0,4,2], derive the exclusive scan [0,3,3,7] and total nine; list each half-open output interval and prove they cannot overlap. Contrast inclusive [3,3,7,9]. Show the overflow condition for a 64-bit unsigned total. Explain why a GPU parallel scan requires group-level communication and additional global coordination, whereas a serial CPU scan needs only one sequential accumulator. Explain Morton key interleaving for coordinates (1,2), yielding nine, and give an example of why Z-order is not globally sorted Euclidean distance.
Sorting needs an input and comparator contract

Compare insertion, selection, bubble, merge, quick, heap, introsort, counting and radix sorting. Include worst-case complexity, memory, stability and suitability for nearly sorted input or small integer keys. Explain why binary and lower-bound search cannot be run on an unsorted range and why NaN comparison without a total-order policy can violate the comparator contract. Give one workload where stable sorting is required and one where ordered iteration is irrelevant.
Dynamic programming, randomized selection and caches

Show why choosing the largest denomination first fails for {1,3,4} and target six, and derive the DP recurrence for the minimum number of coins. Explain when memoization and tabulation produce identical answers but different execution/storage patterns. Prove one-element reservoir sampling uniform by induction; distinguish a fixed random seed from an unbiased generator. Explain the Fisher–Yates swap range. Build an LRU cache from a list plus hash index, trace its eviction at capacity two, then connect stable handles to sparse-set swap-removal and generation checking.
The final performance decision

Given the same asset count and query/update workload, compare an open-addressed table, balanced tree, sorted vector, sparse set and direct-index table. Record correctness invariants and whether iteration pointers survive mutation. Design benchmark distributions over n, hash collisions, hit/miss ratios, entity churn, graph density and memory pressure. Profile before naming a winner. An example-only test is not evidence of expected-case performance for arbitrary production input.

Independent mastery gate: reproduce a FIFO, tombstone probe, heap priority rule, Dijkstra relaxation, topological Kahn step, DSU union and exclusive scan without looking up the source; then explain exactly what breaks when the preconditions fail. The source-to-claim chain should remain inspectable, and no current Kairo code is claimed verified unless actually read.
Recall the recursive cost before naming its theorem

Appendix.title: University - Graphics Vision and Photography - Visual Recall
Appendix.source: Visual Recall/University - Graphics Vision and Photography - Visual Recall.md
Appendix.Content: Worlds, Images and Inference — Fast Recall
Fast route

Start with a world description and follow it through the physical and computational steps that form an image. Then ask what the measurements let us recover about the world. Each step changes representation and may discard information.

ListItem.Content: Represent points, curves, surfaces, and meshes with the data each operation needs.
Place and move geometry with coordinate frames, hierarchies, animation, and simulation.
Measure the scene through optics, exposure, sensors, and camera projection.
Render visible surfaces, material response, and light transport; rasterization and ray queries organize the work differently.
Sample the continuous image with filters and finite pixels, then encode color for a device.
Infer hidden motion, orientation, shape, or object pose from measurements, stating ambiguities and assumptions.

Appendix.Content: For the core visual anchors, open Figure U1; Figure U2; Figure U3; Figure U4; and Figure U5.
Thirty-five retrieval briefs
Each brief gives a mechanism to recall, the condition that matters, and a concrete question to use when reopening that section. The links target the matching chapter in the main note.

ListItem.Content: A scene description becomes an image — Graphics maps a scene description to image measurements; vision works backward from measurements to constraints on the scene. Both depend on camera, geometry, light, and sampling assumptions. Ask: In a ray renderer and a rasterizer, which direction does the visibility query travel?

Mathematical language: points, vectors, and derivatives — A point locates; a vector displaces. In a skew basis, geometric squared length is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>c</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>G</mi> <mi>c</mi> </math>, with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>G</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi>B</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mi>B</mi> </math>. A Jacobian predicts local change; the Hessian records curvature. Ask: Why does summing squared coordinates fail when basis vectors are not orthogonal?

Coordinate frames, transformations, and pose — Homogeneous coordinates let one matrix translate points while leaving direction vectors unchanged. For column vectors, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>T</mi> <mi>S</mi> </math> means scale first, then translate; order matters. Normals use inverse-transpose under nonuniform scale. Ask: What result does <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>S</mi> <mi>T</mi> </math> produce for a point when translation is accidentally scaled too?

Curves as controllable functions — A cubic has four degrees of freedom: endpoint positions and endpoint tangents fit Hermite data. Bézier controls expose tangents; de Casteljau evaluates and subdivides exactly. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>C</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msup> </math> matches parameter speed as well as direction; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>G</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msup> </math> only matches tangent direction. Ask: Why can a visually tangent join still have a speed jump?

Surfaces, patches, topology, and parameterization — A chart maps a parameter domain onto a surface; its partial derivatives span the tangent plane. A chart can distort or become singular even if the surface itself is regular. Ask: What condition on the two tangent vectors makes a parameterization lose a local direction?

Meshes, connectivity, and geometry processing — A mesh stores geometry plus adjacency. Half-edges encode directed edge pairs and make face and vertex neighborhoods traversable. Edits must preserve required topology and orientation. See Figure U2. Ask: After an edge flip, which adjacent face can become inverted if the new diagonal is geometrically invalid?

Lens optics, focus, and image formation — A thin lens maps object distance to image distance; defocus spreads a point into a blur circle. Acceptable focus depends on the blur tolerance and output scale, not a universal depth-of-field boundary. The added derivation estimates a focus interval of about 2.34–4.19 m for its stated setup. Ask: Which chosen circle-of-confusion threshold changes that interval?

Exposure, sensors, and dynamic range — Exposure controls collected photons through aperture, shutter time, and sensitivity; equivalent brightness does not imply equivalent motion blur, depth of field, noise, or highlight headroom. Sensor readout and saturation add limits. Ask: If shutter time is halved and aperture widened one stop, what changes besides image brightness?

Cameras, projection, and calibration — Pinhole projection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>x</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>f</mi> <mi>X</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>Z</mi> </math> couples image scale to depth. Vanishing points constrain parallel directions; calibration estimates internal parameters and pose from known geometry. Orthographic projection is useful when depth variation is negligible or should not affect measured scale. Ask: Why can three orthogonal vanishing directions still leave a mirror-related calibration solution?

Sampling continuous signals and image formation — Sampling records finite values of a continuous signal. Frequencies above half the sample rate can alias to a lower pattern; prefilter before reducing resolution. Pixel-area averaging is already a weak low-pass filter. See Figure U3. Ask: How can two different sinusoids produce identical samples on one grid?

Image sampling, filtering, and efficient reconstruction — Reconstruction filters trade alias suppression, blur, and ringing. A texture Jacobian maps a pixel footprint into texture space; mipmaps suit near-isotropic footprints, anisotropic filters suit elongated ones. Integral images turn any axis-aligned box sum into four table reads after one cumulative pass. Ask: Why does an integral image not make an arbitrary convolution constant-time?

Color perception, encoding, and display — Cone responses compress a spectrum into three values, so distinct spectra can be metamers. Display codes are often nonlinear: decode to linear light before averaging or compositing, then encode for display. Gamut bounds which responses a device can reproduce. Ask: Why does encoded midpoint 0.5 represent roughly 0.22 linear intensity under gamma 2.2?

Light measurement and radiometry — Flux, irradiance, intensity, and radiance use different measures. For an area-light element, conversion from area density to solid-angle density uses <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <msub> <mi>n</mi> <mi>y</mi> </msub> <mo>⋅</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>ω</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mrow> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <msup> <mi>r</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> </math>. Use the same measure as the integral. Ask: Why does sampling an area light require both the inverse-square factor and the light-normal cosine?

Reflectance, BRDFs, and shading — A BRDF describes how incoming direction becomes outgoing radiance. Lambertian reflectance is constant at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>ρ</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>π</mi> </math>; mirrors are delta-like and glossy materials form lobes. Ask: Why can a smooth directional sampler fail to hit an ideal mirror reflection?

The rendering equation and light transport — Outgoing radiance is emitted light plus visible reflected incoming radiance integrated over a hemisphere. Since incoming radiance comes from other surfaces, transport is coupled. A renderer makes this executable with visibility, BRDF, light, and accumulation. See Figure U5. Ask: Which term becomes zero when geometry blocks a sampled direction?

Numerical integration and Monte Carlo estimation — For samples <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>X</mi> <mo>∼</mo> <mi>p</mi> </math>, estimate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∫</mo> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>d</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math> with the mean of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Importance sampling reduces estimator variance only when the density covers every contributing region. Ask: Why does quadrupling independent samples usually halve standard error rather than quarter it?

Rasterization, coverage, and depth — Rasterization tests projected primitives at pixel sample locations, interpolates attributes, then depth-tests. Exact edge coverage is an area integral; multisampling estimates it with subpixel tests. Perspective-correct interpolation compensates for the projection divide. Ask: What artifact appears if a checkerboard floor is linearly interpolated in screen space?

Textures and surface detail — Texture is a signal over surface coordinates. Charts introduce seams and distortion; filtering must follow how that domain projects into each pixel. Ask: Why can one square mip level overblur a floor receding toward the horizon?

Visibility queries and ray intersections — A ray query asks which geometry intersects a path from an origin; hit parameters, barycentric coordinates, and surface orientation answer different parts of the intersection contract. Ask: What additional bound distinguishes a ray from a finite line segment?

Acceleration structures and robust queries — A BVH groups geometry in nested bounds. Traversal skips a node only when its bound cannot intersect the query, so bounds must conservatively contain descendants. Robust predicates matter near tangencies and degenerate geometry. Ask: What correctness failure follows from rounding a bound inward?

Scene graphs and articulated geometry — A node’s world transform composes parent and local transforms; skinning blends posed bone candidates using per-vertex weights. Linear blends can collapse volume when averaging opposing rotations. Ask: Why does applying the inverse bind transform preserve a vertex when current pose equals rest pose?

Animation curves and motion paths — A moving camera needs position and orientation, plus a valid up direction. Smooth position does not guarantee smooth orientation; rotation interpolation and time parameterization are separate choices. Ask: What makes the camera frame singular when view and up vectors align?

Dynamics, forces, and numerical integration — Dynamics evolves state from forces or interaction rules; an integrator approximates continuous time with steps. Large steps can inject energy or destabilize springs and cloth. Ask: Why can explicit Euler make a spring oscillation grow even when the physical model conserves energy?

Optimization, constraints, and inverse kinematics — Define variables, objective, constraints, and derivatives before solving. IK linearizes forward kinematics with a Jacobian; feasibility and conditioning govern whether a target is reachable and stable. Ask: What changes when the end-effector Jacobian loses rank?

PDEs, fields, and discrete solvers — A PDE, spatial discretization, and boundary conditions together define a numerical problem. Choosing a mesh or basis changes the system matrix; boundary data is part of the model. Ask: Why can two solvers using the same interior equation produce different solutions at the boundary?

Optical flow and motion from images — Brightness constancy yields one equation, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mi>x</mi> </msub> <mi>u</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mi>y</mi> </msub> <mi>v</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math>, for two flow components. A local aperture therefore leaves motion along an edge ambiguous. Ask: What does a single straight edge constrain well, and which motion component remains unobserved?

Edges, contours, and subpixel localization — Blur spreads an ideal edge; fitting a response profile can estimate its center between pixels. Hough voting accumulates weak local evidence into a global line or shape hypothesis. Ask: Why can an edge’s subpixel estimate shift when the blur model is wrong?

Recognition, templates, and industrial matching — Template matching searches over pose and transformation with a score chosen for expected noise and deformation. Coarse-to-fine search reduces cost; thresholds set tolerance, not truth. Ask: Why should an edge alignment score treat normal displacement differently from tangent displacement?

Pose estimation, transforms, and robust fitting — Estimate rigid pose from correspondences, enforce a proper rotation, and use robust fitting when outliers contaminate matches. RANSAC trial count depends on inlier rate and sample size. Ask: Why does lowering the assumed inlier fraction sharply increase the number of RANSAC trials?

Stereo, relative orientation, and reconstruction — Two views constrain rays and relative pose; triangulation recovers structure up to gauge freedoms such as global scale. Critical surfaces make the geometry ill-conditioned. Ask: Why can perfect image correspondences still leave metric scale unknown?

Surface orientation from illumination — Photometric stereo uses several known light directions to solve for scaled normal from brightness measurements. The lighting matrix must span the components being estimated. See Figure U4. Ask: Which normal component becomes unobservable if every light direction lies in one plane?

Shape from shading and reflectance — A single shading image gives a nonlinear relation among surface normal, reflectance, and illumination; integration into height requires boundary conditions and extra assumptions. Ask: Why does a locally valid normal field fail to guarantee one globally consistent surface?

Surface descriptions and Gaussian images — A Gaussian image maps surface area to normal directions. Its directional mass distribution summarizes orientation and curvature patterns but can be shared by geometrically different surfaces. Ask: Why does the zero-centroid condition hold for a closed surface, and what does it rule out?

Photographic composition, history, and communication — Viewpoint, crop, sequence, and caption shape how a photograph functions as evidence or argument. A recorded scene is selected and framed, not a neutral inventory. Ask: What does a wide frame reveal that a close crop hides in the same documentary image?

Photographic workflow and integrated decisions — Trace a capture from scene spectrum through optics, exposure, sampling, processing, and display. Each stage can discard information or add artifacts; choose settings around the intended output. Ask: Which stage caused a moiré pattern, and what evidence distinguishes it from JPEG blocking?

Appendix.Content: Evidence and scope

The source ledger covers 88 entries: 70 requested lectures and 18 added sources. Its evidence includes 86 published English automatic-caption tracks, one locally generated Whisper transcript for a technical lecture, one sampled showcase video, and 70 lecture PDFs matched to their course years. Captions, notes, and sampled visuals support different claims; the legend records which evidence supports each entry.

These briefs are deliberately compact retrieval notes for a 35-chapter continuous treatment. They are not a transcript, a substitute for the worked derivations, or a claim that the entire companion fits on one physical page.
Four more figures to redraw from memory
New mechanisms to retrieve

A vertex buffer is a byte array interpreted by a draw command. The stride says how many bytes separate successive vertices; the attribute offset says where one field begins inside a vertex. Rasterization and vertex layout · U10. Ask: For 24-byte float32 vertices with RGB after XYZ, what are the position stride and color offset?

A mathematical projection of a finite point set is a map to a line. Small image size means many collisions. Scale, spacing, and additive structure determine whether many directions can compress the same set. This is separate from a camera’s projection matrix. Finite-field collisions · Real projection scales · U11. Ask: Is the obstruction arithmetic, spatial clustering, or an incidence pattern?

A classifier maps an image representation to scores; a loss compares those scores with the target. The gradient sends a local change backward through each operation by the chain rule. Convolution shares a local filter over the image; attention instead builds content-dependent weights between tokens. Learning basics · CNNs · Attention. Ask: Which shape changes at each layer, and where does the chain rule multiply upstream and local derivatives?

Dense prediction assigns an output to every pixel; detection also predicts object locations and categories. Video adds temporal alignment, motion, and compute cost. Dense prediction and detection · Video. Ask: Does the evaluation measure pixel accuracy, object matching, or temporal consistency?

Self-supervision creates training targets from the data; generative objectives instead define how a model represents or samples possible outputs. Evaluation must match the claim: reconstruction quality, likelihood, sample quality, and downstream usefulness are different measurements. Self-supervision · Generative models. Ask: What observable target trains the model, and what test would falsify the capability claim?

NeRF represents a scene with a learned field queried along rays; Gaussian splatting stores explicit 3D elements and composites their projected contributions. A planar Gaussian gives a direct local surface normal, while 3D Gaussian splats need geometric regularization to recover reliable surfaces. Learned 3D representations · research methods · U12 · U13. Ask: Which representation is queried per ray and which is explicitly rasterized?

An environment map supplies incoming illumination by direction. ReSTIR uses weighted reservoirs to reuse light candidates, but the final estimator still needs correct proposal support and normalization. LoD changes also change geometry, so reused paths need a surface correspondence and its area Jacobian. Image-based lighting · Monte Carlo reuse · U14. Ask: What distribution was each candidate drawn from, and what normalization makes reuse valid?

Mitsuba 2 shows how a renderer can change execution mode and differentiate through image formation. It is a 2019 Enoki-based system; its API details are historical and should not be treated as Mitsuba 3 guidance. Differentiable rendering. Ask: Which quantities are differentiated and which sampling decisions are held fixed?

ARAP editing alternates local rigid rotations with a global sparse position solve. Field-aligned remeshing uses orientation and position fields to guide edge direction and placement. Mesh processing. Ask: Which part is local per vertex and which system is solved globally?

IPC combines a contact barrier with continuous collision detection and a feasibility-preserving line search. A positive barrier alone is not a proof that a finite time step cannot cross a contact. Contact dynamics · U15. Ask: What checks the entire path between the current and proposed configurations?

Read the loop as a diagnostic map: representation, forward model, objective, and evaluation can each limit the result. It is not a single training algorithm; Monte Carlo rendering and supervised learning use different estimators and losses.
This rendering/inference loop joins the original image-formation chapters to learned 3D methods. The reverse arrow indicates an inference problem; it does not imply a unique reconstruction.
Rendering, materials, transport — retrieve the reasons

The left panel explains projective interpolation; the middle separates encoded storage from linear light; the right proves that a missing sampling region can create bias. These are numerical witnesses, not rendered screenshots from a working engine.

Cell.Content: A primitive can cross the camera plane; division near zero creates unbounded coordinates. Clip the homogeneous primitive first.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Decide which samples a triangle owns
Which barycentrics recover a texture coordinate?
Screen weights need reciprocal-<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> </math> correction. Already-divided depth instead interpolates affinely on screen.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Decide which samples a triangle owns
Reciprocal distance pairs well with floating-point spacing near zero; every depth consumer must agree on ordering.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Give depth an explicit meaning
Why is encoded midpoint <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>0.5</mn> </math> too dark?
It decodes to about <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>0.214</mn> </math> linear light. Average linear values first.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Make every color number carry a meaning
Facet distribution, interface reflection, and geometric visibility. The NDF normalizes with projected area.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Ask a surface where incoming energy can go
Why can a PDF exceed one?
It is density per unit measure. Its integral is one; its pointwise value need not be bounded by one.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Follow one path without losing its probability
Light-choice probability, area density, and the area-to-solid-angle Jacobian.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Follow one path without losing its probability
Correctly weighted contributions from the participating sampling techniques, in the same measure, with delta events handled separately.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Follow one path without losing its probability
Does more sampling remove every error?
It reduces stochastic error under the estimator’s assumptions. Missing-domain and transport-model bias can remain.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#A missing region cannot be repaired by taking more samples there

Appendix.Content: Reconstruct without looking: show why the screen midpoint gives <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>u</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.2</mn> </math> for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>; derive the cosine hemisphere integral <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>π</mi> </math>; convert a selected area-light density into solid angle; explain why roulette survivors divide by survival probability. Then point to where each assumption appears in the implementation.
Explicit rendering, captured kernels and animated surfaces - retrieval briefs

ListItem.Content: Covariance to pixels — A Jacobian is a local linear prediction. Transform covariance as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>J</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>J</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math>, then invert the 2D covariance for the conic. Near-plane rejection and a finite footprint policy are prerequisites. Why is this only a local perspective approximation?

Allocate tile work — Count references, exclusive-scan counts, scatter to disjoint slices, sort by tile/depth, then composite. Counts <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math> give offsets <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>6</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>11</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math>. Why must an unstable final tile sort not destroy depth order?

Composite in order — Contribution is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>T</mi> <mi>α</mi> <mi>c</mi> </math> and new transmittance is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>T</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>−</mo> <mi>α</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Two half-opaque layers leave <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>T</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.25</mn> </math>. A transmittance threshold is an approximation budget, not a universal reference constant.

Validate separate outputs — Compare color in a declared space, depth with units, and IDs as discrete values. Average error, peak error and changed-pixel fraction answer different questions. CPU/GPU agreement does not establish antialiasing quality.

Reuse the right object — A slot fence proves slot work completed. It does not prove a presentation wait consumed its semaphore. Frame-slot and acquired-image indices are separate domains. What resolves an acquisition followed by recording failure?

Retire across queues — Every required queue counter must be reached. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>10</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>100</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> does not cover required <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>9</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Ownership preserves the payload; completion permits destruction.

Compile the graph — Versions identify values, dependencies order producers/consumers, and lifetimes constrain storage aliasing. A list position does not prove that independent queues have stopped using memory.

Turn capture into editable world — Persistent identity survives sorting; physical support supplies deformation. For affine motion, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>μ</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mi>F</mi> <mi>μ</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>t</mi> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mi>F</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>F</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math>. Appearance kernels alone supply neither mass nor colliders.

Animate in a declared space — Sample pose, resolve the hierarchy, morph before skinning, and build matching current/previous transforms. A global-joint palette already outputs world space. Why does adding the mesh world transform again break it?

Image-change bounds need assumptions — An opacity-only bound misses a red-to-blue edit at fixed opacity and a depth-order swap. State color range, evaluated per-pixel alpha changes, contributor order, color/background changes, and termination policy before calling an estimate a certificate.

Cell.Content: Flat index is valid; coordinates valid?
Not necessarily. At width 800, x=800,y=0 spills into the next row. Check each coordinate before indexing.

Clear each frame or retain pixels?

Cell.Content: Perpendicular distance to an infinite line; no endpoint, frustum or occlusion test.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#A line corridor can be a cheap prefilter for shadow-caster work
When is rejecting a caster safe?
The corridor must enclose its possible contribution region; the object sphere must enclose transformed geometry.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#A line corridor can be a cheap prefilter for shadow-caster work
Center distance above 0.9 rejects. A smaller distance only retains a candidate.
Largest matrix column bounds every stretch?
No under shear: a 1.414 guess misses a 1.618 stretch. Frobenius radius multiplier 2 is safe here.

Mesh energy and value range

Cell.Content: Can a negative cotangent edge weight coexist with nonnegative energy?
Yes. Valid element energies are squared gradients; individual signed edge terms are coupled by geometry.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Nonnegative energy and nonnegative weights are different promises
Does a stable heat step preserve nonnegative values?
Not necessarily: the worked step produces −0.015 while energy falls from 0.125 to 0.104525.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#A stable heat step can still create a negative sample
What makes an explicit diffusion update a convex average?
Nonnegative edge weights, positive lumped masses, and a step small enough to keep every diagonal update coefficient nonnegative.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Complete single-triangle energy witness

Cell.Content: What makes the planar camera bearing model valid?
Known landmarks, planar motion and the explicitly identity body-to-camera extrinsic.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Make the visual correction small enough to inspect: an eight-state planar EKF
High-rate samples between keyframes into declared relative motion summaries; it is not a complete visual estimator.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#From raw 3-D IMU samples to the pose constraint used by VIO

Segment opacity and remaining transmittance weight emitted sample colors.

Each arrow that transfers device-produced data needs the API’s required dependency. Finishing a dispatch alone does not replace memory visibility.

Cell.Content: Is an append ticket a stored record?
Only when it fits. Track attempted count, stored count and overflow; reject an incomplete candidate structure.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Build GPU bins and fixed hash tables only after capacity and ownership are explicit
Count entries, scan counts into disjoint starts, then scatter within each owned bin interval. Atomic arrival order can vary.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Worked 2D spatial-bin build
What does CAS publish in the small hash model?
It claims a key slot for one payload writer. Queries wait for the whole build and memory handoff.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Fixed-capacity open addressing with a bounded build pass
How does a full table terminate?
Probe at most its capacity; report failure and rebuild or reject.

Cell.Content: Its final consumer’s completed token; cycling a slot index proves nothing.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Double and triple buffering change ownership, not execution speed
Can async compute always overlap a draw?
Only if dependencies and resource contention permit. Two queues do not imply independent execution hardware.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Async compute starts with a dependency graph
No. Mapping, cache visibility and consumer completion are different conditions.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Uploads need bandwidth, visibility and retirement
The smaller of arithmetic peak and bandwidth × arithmetic intensity, with matching units and memory boundary.
[[Continuous Notes/University - Worlds, Images and Inference - Graphics, Vision and Photography#Derive a roofline bound with matching units
Why can FP16 lose a unit increment at 2048?
Neighbor spacing is 2; 2049 rounds to 2048 under ties-to-even. Widening later cannot restore lost input.

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Barycentric coordinates and interpolation — Barycentric coordinates and interpolation Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism Barycentric weights reconstruct a triangle point as an affine combination. The weights sum to one; nonnegative weights describe points inside or on a nondegenerate triangle. Dot-system solves on off-plane inputs describe their projection, not proven surface membership. The panel sensor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> has weights <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>12</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and corner temperatures <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>20</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>40</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>50</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> interpolate to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>35</mn> </math>. Source and navigation Teaching narrative · Coverage and source gap · Evidence and limits · Dependency Map University course development Extend the existing interpolation note with the geometric meanings that make triangle rasterization and camera calibration easier to reason about. For triangle vertices <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </math>, a point inside can be written <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>λ</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>p</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> </math>, where the weights sum to one and are nonnegative. Each weight is the area of the opposite subtriangle divided by the full triangle area; equivalently it is a signed edge-distance normalized by altitude. The weights therefore provide both a point-in-triangle test and attribute interpolation. They also reveal a limitation: screen-space weights do not linearly interpolate a 3D attribute after perspective projection. Interpolate reciprocal depth and attribute divided by depth, then divide the interpolated values to recover perspective-correct texture coordinates or colors. Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Temporal reprojection and history validation — Temporal reprojection and history validation Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: XR01 · Latest development: XR01 Definition and mechanism Reprojection aligns history with a current target; disocclusion exposes content with no matching old observation. Validated blending trades noise against response/ghosting. Gaze-driven quality changes also change history reliability; TAA is not exposure integration. Prerequisites
Spatiotemporal sampling and retinal motion — Temporal reuse must respect changing scene and retinal observations. Antialiasing and sample allocation — History depends on the actual current/prior sampling strategy.
Used by
Foveated rendering and uncertainty Reservoir resampling and ReSTIR ## Recall and next depth
Derive ideal history variance and identify every violated assumption. Pending: motion/depth/jitter conventions and robust implementation. Written coverage is not a claim of learner mastery or accepted numbered-curriculum progress. Source and navigation Expanded teaching explanation · Independent coverage · Dependency Map Phase 11 camera development Reprojection predicts where a prior sample lands under camera and object motion. Depth agreement tests whether the same visible surface likely occupies that location, but cannot prove stored color remains valid after lighting, exposure, material, or sampling changes. Combine projected position, depth tolerance, and disocclusion checks; reduce history weight when confidence is low. Monocular reconstruction has arbitrary global scale, so metric depth thresholds require an external scale or consistent units. Reprojection success is geometric evidence, not a photometric guarantee. Link: A camera model must close the loop; research: Four deeper links from the TUM lecture review. Neighborhood clipping and deterministic jitter witness tools/labs/realtime_effects_reference_lab.cpp now extends history validity into two mechanisms that directly affect temporal stability. The first is deterministic subpixel jitter generated from Halton bases 2 and 3. The sample lies inside one pixel but changes frame to frame, allowing temporal accumulation to observe different subpixel locations. A jitter sequence must be owned by the camera/projection history contract: if the current and previous transforms disagree about whether jitter is included, the motion vector and reprojection become inconsistent. The second is neighborhood clipping. A reprojected history value can be geometrically valid yet photometrically stale after disocclusion or fast shading change. The smallest CPU oracle clamps the history sample into the current 3×3 neighborhood min/max interval before blending. Production TAA often uses variance-guided bounds, color-space transforms, reactive masks and velocity-dependent weighting, but the invariant remains: history should not inject values unsupported by the current local evidence. The laboratory checks known first Halton points, uniqueness over an initial sequence, bright/dark history rejection and preservation of an in-range history value. It remains a semantic oracle rather than a complete production TAA implementation.. Open Temporal reprojection and history validation in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Tensor-product interpolation — Tensor-product interpolation Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Bilinear and trilinear interpolation apply one-dimensional linear weights independently along each coordinate axis. In a rectangular cell, each corner contributes the product of its axis weights; the weights are nonnegative and sum to one for coordinates inside the cell. This preserves the range of scalar corner values, but the interpolated surface can be twisted rather than planar, and derivatives may jump across cell boundaries. For a voxel field, trilinear interpolation provides a continuous in-cell estimate; differentiating it yields a local gradient, which need not have unit length even when samples approximate signed distance. Keep coordinates normalized to the cell and define behavior outside the sampled grid explicitly. Prerequisites
Interpolation versus approximation Sampling aliasing and reconstruction

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 1, The Engine Builder's Bible — Volume I: From First Frame to Core Runtime Systems: Storage duration and object lifetime — Storage duration and object lifetime Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C010 Definition and mechanism Direct local reference binding can extend a temporary under specified rules; a returned parameter alias does not renew the deadline. A reference’s own lifetime does not prove the referent’s lifetime. Construction and destruction can delimit an occupant while backing storage remains. The inline C++ lab uses construct_at/destroy_at in an alignas byte buffer and new/delete as the combined allocation/construction and destruction/release operations. The pointer object does not own or extend pointee life. Implicit object creation occurs only for specified operations and suitable types; a reinterpret_cast is not a universal construction operation. Storage duration specifies how long storage is potentially available: automatic, static, thread, or dynamic. Object lifetime describes when a particular initialized object exists within it. Old bytes can remain after lifetime ends without authorizing access. const restricts mutation, not physical placement. Language categories do not dictate a universal segment map. M010 reuses this separation for smart owners and arenas: a wrapper’s storage duration, the managed object’s lifetime, the ownership-group lifetime, and an external GPU-use interval may all end at different times. The eigenspace is the null space of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mi>λ</mi> <mi>I</mi> </math>. Real symmetric matrices have an orthonormal eigenbasis; general matrices may be defective or have sensitive eigenvectors. This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Interpolation versus approximation — Interpolation versus approximation Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Interpolation reproduces every prescribed sample exactly, while approximation minimizes or controls an error criterion and may miss the observations. The distinction matters when data are noisy: a high-degree interpolant can fit measurement noise and oscillate between samples, while a lower-complexity approximation can better represent the underlying trend. In texture reconstruction, the samples themselves often define the represented signal, so interpolation is an appropriate reconstruction rule. In calibration, observations have uncertainty, so fitting a model may be more defensible. Neither method is automatically superior; choose based on the meaning of the data, the error measure, and whether evaluation stays within or extrapolates beyond the sampled domain. Prerequisites
Taylor models and approximation error Barycentric coordinates and interpolation

A subspace retains these operations inside a larger space. The span of generators is every finite linear combination of them. The plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>z</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> is a subspace of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> </msup> </math>; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>z</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> is an affine translate, not a subspace. The span of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> contains all in-plane movements. This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Uniform shuffling without replacement — Uniform shuffling without replacement Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Fisher–Yates generates a uniform permutation by walking from the last array element downward and choosing an index uniformly from the unshuffled prefix. Each permutation has probability <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mo>!</mo> </math> if every bounded integer choice is unbiased and the random source meets its assumptions. A common error is to use a random integer routine with modulo bias; another is to draw from the wrong interval and omit permutations. For a fixed input array, test that the output contains every original element once; statistical tests can supplement, but not replace, deterministic checks of bounds and uniqueness. The same primitive supports uniform sample subsets and randomized stratification. Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: ODE integration and stability — ODE integration and stability Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism An ordinary differential equation gives the rate of change of a state over time. Forward Euler uses the current derivative: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi>k</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>t</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>h</mi> </math> is the time step. For decay <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mover> <mi>u</mi> <mo>˙</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mi>u</mi> </math>, it multiplies each step by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> <mo>−</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mi>h</mi> </math>; if the magnitude exceeds one, the numerical solution grows even though the true solution decays. Spring systems can be stiff because high-frequency modes force very small stable steps. Backward Euler evaluates the rate at the unknown new state and is more stable for decay but requires solving an equation and may add numerical damping. Symplectic Euler updates velocity then position and often keeps energy bounded for conservative mechanics. Choose an integrator according to stability, accuracy, conservation, and runtime rather than displayed frame rate alone. Phase 9–10 development An initial-value problem consists of a differential equation and a specified starting state. A numerical integrator replaces continuous evolution with finite updates, so accuracy and stability depend on both method and step size. Consistency concerns local approximation, stability concerns error growth under repeated steps, and convergence concerns the limiting solution as the step is refined. Stiff systems can force explicit methods to take very small steps even when the visible trajectory changes slowly. Symplectic methods preserve Hamiltonian structure but do not generally preserve exact energy at each step. Prerequisites
Absolute and relative error Conditioning and singularity ODE initial-value problems and stiffness Time integrators and symplectic updates
Used by
Worlds, Images and Inference Implicit differentiation and parameter sensitivities
Full teaching explanation Dynamics, forces, and numerical integration · Animation curves and motion paths - Phase 9 teaching section - Visual Recall/09 - Calculus and Optimization - Visual Recall.md · Phase 9 visual recall. Open ODE integration and stability in Volume 2

Changing description uses the inverse destination frame followed by the source frame; active motion and passive coordinate change answer different questions. Fixing one camera pose chooses a world origin and orientation, but adds no image evidence. Monocular scale remains free until a baseline, known length, or metric sensor anchors it. Do not mistake a coordinate convention for an empirical measurement. This distinction matters when defining bundle-adjustment priors and covariance, and assumes a rigid calibrated camera model. Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Camera view and clip-space pipeline — Camera view and clip-space pipeline Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase7 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism A camera pose maps camera coordinates to world coordinates; its inverse is the view map. Projection produces homogeneous clip coordinates, clipping applies the API-specific inequalities, and valid perspective division produces NDC. Storage order supplies none of these coordinate contracts. Reconstruction cue: A standard minus-Z perspective example needs a point in front of the camera and a meaningful clip w before division. Prerequisites
Coordinate frames and change of basis
Used by
Phase 7 teaching and laboratory Depth buffering and visibility order Lens optics and depth of field GPU vertex specification Homogeneous clipping and perspective interpolation Axial depth and Euclidean range Hardware depth-buffer linearization Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking Ray differentials and camera sampling measures
Recall and next depth Reconstruct the example, state its conventions and find an input that violates its preconditions. Deeper algorithms and measured production performance remain separate from the present model. Source and navigation Continuous explanation · Coverage and source gap · Sources and verification University course development Extend the existing transform pipeline with the clipping and depth-precision decisions that make projection robust. A view frustum is the set of points a camera can see, bounded by near and far planes as well as image sides. Transforming the frustum into a canonical clip cube makes outside tests cheap; partially intersecting triangles must be clipped and triangulated so the rasterizer still receives triangles. The near plane also avoids geometry crossing the eye plane, while the far plane limits depth range. Floating-point depth values are unevenly distributed after perspective division, so an excessively tiny near distance paired with a huge far distance can make two nearby surfaces quantize to the same depth and produce z-fighting. Choose the narrowest useful depth interval and keep the view, clip, normalized, and screen coordinates distinct. A scene description becomes an image · Cameras, projection, and calibration · Rasterization, coverage, and depth Phase 11 camera development A raster-to-ray camera maps a pixel to a geometric sample; In a pinhole model, invert projection and view transforms to recover a camera-space direction, then transform it to world space without applying translation as if it were a point. Pixel-center convention, viewport origin, handedness, clip-depth range, and normalization all affect the result. Offset a pixel to generate differential rays and estimate the surface footprint; that footprint grows with depth and changes with surface orientation. Keep ray generation distinct from raster projection while ensuring their conventions agree. Link: A camera model must close the loop; research: Four deeper links from the TUM lecture review.. Open Camera view and clip-space pipeline in Volume 2

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Latin-hypercube sampling — Latin-hypercube sampling Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10 Definition and mechanism Latin-hypercube sampling divides each coordinate axis into <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>N</mi> </math> equal strata and uses a permutation so every sample occupies one stratum per dimension. With randomized within-stratum positions and randomized permutations, each sample has uniform marginal coordinates; samples are dependent by design. This can improve coverage for some integrands at arbitrary sample counts, including counts that do not form a square grid. It does not guarantee lower variance for every function, and IID variance formulas cannot be applied without accounting for dependence. Test exact stratum coverage deterministically, then compare estimator error over repeated randomized trials for the intended integrand. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>N</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>5</mn> </math>, each axis still receives five strata, avoiding the missing-cell bias of taking five cells from a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> <mo>×</mo> <mn>3</mn> </math> grid. Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content: This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Singular value decomposition — Singular value decomposition For any real rectangular matrix, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math>. Right singular vectors are input directions, left singular vectors are output directions, and nonnegative singular values are principal stretches. Unlike eigenvectors, the two sets live in different spaces. Use it when: revealing rank and conditioning, solving rank-uncertain least squares, compressing a matrix, or understanding PCA. Developed in Phase 8: The SVD expresses a rectangular map using orthonormal input and output directions joined by nonnegative stretches. Full, thin, and compact shapes have different dimensions; bidiagonal reduction and Jacobi methods compute the factors, and reconstruction, orthogonality, and triplet residuals check them independently. factor shapes · SVD algorithms and validation Prerequisites Matrix multiplication and composition order, Eigenvalues and eigenspaces, Dot products and orthogonality. Used by Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, PCA and covariance eigensystems, Polar decomposition, Matrix factorization choices. Teaching path: SVD geometry. - Matrix norms and numerical error — Extends this foundation into the Phase 8 dependency spine. - Camera calibration and bundle adjustment - Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics University course development Extend the existing factorization note with its role in estimation, conditioning, and geometry. For matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math>, the decomposition <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math> separates orthogonal input directions, axis-aligned scaling, and orthogonal output directions. Singular values on the diagonal of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> </math> quantify how strongly each independent direction is preserved; a zero or tiny value signals rank loss or poor conditioning. Least-squares fitting can use this structure to identify which parameter combinations are well constrained and to avoid amplifying measurement noise along nearly invisible directions. The same analysis explains why a camera calibration or bundle-adjustment system can have gauge freedoms: translating or scaling the entire reconstruction may leave image measurements unchanged. Singular values diagnose these ambiguities, while constraints or fixed reference poses remove them. Thus SVD links linear algebra to robust vision, not just matrix compression. Pose estimation, transforms, and robust fitting · Stereo, relative orientation, and reconstruction · Optimization, constraints, and inverse kinematics. Open Singular value decomposition in Volume 2

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Minkowski sums and support mappings — Minkowski sums and support mappings Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6 Definition and mechanism Minkowski addition combines pairwise position coordinates of sets in a common frame. Collision difference means <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>B</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> here. A support function returns an extreme scalar measurement; a support mapping returns a maximizing point, possibly with ties. Intervals <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math> have difference <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">[</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">]</mo> </math>, containing zero. Support of the difference uses a support point of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math> minus one of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> </math> queried in the opposite direction. Prerequisites
